expected: A finding that identifies priority.upper() being called before any null/missing check, causing AttributeError (HTTP 500) when priority is absent or null.
reproduction: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/tickets -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title": "Test"}' — returns HTTP 500 instead of 400.

expected: A finding that identifies no allowed-value check after uppercasing, so arbitrary strings like 'URGENT' are accepted and stored.
reproduction: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/tickets -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title": "Test", "priority": "URGENT"}' — returns 201 and stores 'URGENT'.

expected: A finding that no test asserts the missing/null-priority behaviour (expected: 400 invalid_priority; actual: 500 AttributeError).
reproduction: No test exists that calls POST /tickets without a priority field and asserts status 400 with error 'invalid_priority'.

expected: A finding that no test asserts the unsupported-priority behaviour (expected: 400 invalid_priority; actual: 201 accepted).
reproduction: No test exists that calls POST /tickets with priority='URGENT' and asserts status 400 with error 'invalid_priority'.

expected: A finding that docs/api.md does not mention the priority field on POST /tickets (request or response) and does not document the invalid_priority error code.
reproduction: Search docs/api.md for 'priority' — no match. The field and its error are completely absent from the API contract.

expected: A finding that the title length check uses >= instead of >, rejecting titles of exactly 100 characters which the API contract allows.
reproduction: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/tickets -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"title": "'$(python3 -c "print('a'*100)"'"}' — returns 400 instead of 201.
